Officer's narrative
Driver 1 was traveling northbound in the left-hand lane on a city street in Pasadena, Texas, and was turning left at the
intersection when the collision occurred. Driver 2 was southbound and proceeded through the intersection, striking
the left side of Driver 1's vehicle. A passenger was seated in the front passenger seat of Driver 1's vehicle at the time
of impact. Both drivers remained at the scene, and the passenger was present and confirmed by officers and
independent witnesses as being inside the vehicle during the collision. Driver 1 reported neck pain consistent with
whiplash, which is a plausible injury for a side impact of this type. Several witnesses stated that the collision
happened as both drivers described it, and photographs taken at the scene were consistent with their accounts. The
damage to Driver 1's vehicle, located along the left side and rear quarter panel, matches the direction and force of the
impact described. No prior damage to the vehicle was known to officers or to the parties involved. Driver 1 is the
named insured on the policy covering the vehicle. No citations were issued at the scene, and both parties exchanged
insurance information before leaving.
